Sabbaba
Business Profile & Notes — Bondi Junction (Spring St) location
This is a plain-language write-up of everything publicly findable about Sabbaba's Bondi Junction
restaurant, put together the way a business owner might describe their own place in an intake form — in
paragraphs, not spreadsheets. It's meant to sit alongside the structured Excel workbook as unstructured
training/testing input: the same facts, in prose. Anywhere the research turned up a contradiction or a gap,
it's called out in the text rather than smoothed over, so a reader (or a model) can decide how to handle it.
Compiled 4 September 2026, from the Uber Eats storefront, Google Places, TripAdvisor, Yelp, HappyCow,
abillion, Wanderlog and Time Out Sydney.
About Sabbaba
Sabbaba is a fast-casual Middle Eastern and Israeli restaurant built around falafel, pita pockets, grilled
meats and big customisable plates of salads and dips. The name itself is a bit of a mission statement — in
Hebrew slang, "sabbaba" means something like "cool" or "no worries," and the brand's own marketing
leans into that relaxed, casual identity. The food style pulls from across the Mediterranean and North
Africa: a Tunisian pita gets Marrakech-style salad and sweet potato, an Algerian pita leans on chickpeas
and eggplant, and there's even a "Cancun" pita that swaps in guacamole, jalapeños and corn chips — so
the menu isn't strictly traditional, it's more "globe-trotting falafel shop."
By most accounts the brand started on Hall Street in Bondi Beach and has since grown into at least two
more Sydney outlets, one of them at Bondi Junction. Reviewers on TripAdvisor even talk about the original
Bondi Beach shop physically relocating from Hall Street to Campbell Parade around 2019, closer to the
beach promenade.
Locations we found
Bondi Junction — Spring Street (Eastgate Bondi Junction shopping centre). This is the location the
original Uber Eats link points to, and the main subject of this profile. Uber Eats lists the address as 77
Spring Street, Bondi Junction NSW 2022; Google's own listing for what appears to be the same storefront
says 91 Spring St; other directories cite ranges like 71–91 or 55–91 Spring Street. That's a wide enough
spread that it's worth just asking the owner for the exact shop number rather than guessing.
Bondi Junction — Westfield / Oxford Street. A second Bondi Junction listing turned up on abillion, at
Level 5, 500 Oxford Street (elsewhere described as Shop 6007, Level 6). It's not clear from public data
whether this is a genuinely separate restaurant or just a different entrance/floor reference for a food-court
counter in the same complex.
Bondi Beach — Hall Street / Campbell Parade. Widely described as the original Sabbaba, and still
showing up under both an old address (82 Hall St) and a newer one (152–162 Campbell Parade),
consistent with the relocation reviewers mention. This location has its own, separate
Google/TripAdvisor/Yelp presence and shouldn't be blended with the Spring Street numbers.
Because there appear to be multiple storefronts, this document tries to keep the Spring Street data clearly
separated from the Bondi Beach and Westfield data. Where a fact could only be confirmed for a location other
than Spring Street, that's noted in the text.


Contact & Practical Details (Spring Street location)
Address: 77 Spring Street, Bondi Junction NSW 2022 (per Uber Eats) — also seen as 91 Spring St
(Google) and 71–91 Spring St (other directories).
Phone: +61 493 872 535 (Google Business listing) — an older number, (02) 9369 5599, also appears on
Yelp for what looks like this same storefront.
Website: sabbaba.com.au — referenced consistently by Yelp, HappyCow and GrubFinder, but the site
blocks automated access, so its current content couldn't be checked directly for this profile.
Ordering: Available on Uber Eats (source of this profile) and listed on the order-ahead app Hey You. Not
confirmed on DoorDash or Menulog.
Price point: "$" — budget/inexpensive, consistently across every platform that rates price level.
Cuisine tags: Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, Israeli, Falafel, Kebab, Salads, Bowls, Vegan,
Vegan-friendly, Vegetarian.
One odd detail worth flagging: the description text Uber Eats itself displays for this store opens with "Sabbaba in
Bondi Beach, Sydney, offers a healthy dining experience..." — even though the address on the same page is
Bondi Junction. That reads like a copy-paste error, possibly reusing another Sabbaba location's blurb, and is
probably worth flagging to Uber Eats merchant support.
Opening Hours
Hours are one of the messier parts of this dataset. Uber Eats shows an 11:00 AM start every day, closing
around 8:00 PM on weekdays and stretching later on some days (with what look like separate "alternate"
and "public holiday" schedules overlapping on the same page — Friday and Saturday, for instance, show
both an 8:00 PM and an 8:30 PM close, and several days show an 11:00 PM "holiday" window). Google's
listing for the same address, on the other hand, shows a 6:00 AM opening every day of the week, which
doesn't fit a lunch-and-dinner Mediterranean menu — it looks like stale data, possibly left over from a
previous café tenant at the same address.
The safest read: expect roughly an 11:00 AM–8:00 PM window most days, but treat the exact daily hours and
any holiday variations as unconfirmed until the owner supplies a current schedule.


The Menu
The Uber Eats menu for the Spring Street store is built around three core formats — a Pita Pocket, a Bowl,
and a Plate — which are really the same core of salads and dips (village salad, tabouli, red cabbage and
pickles, plus hummus, tahini, babaganoush and salsa) served three different ways. The Plate and Pita
Pocket both run $20–$30 and come with one pita; the Bowl is $27 and comes with pita on the side instead
of wrapped in. For $37, the Super Plate steps things up with a choice of two proteins, four seasonal salads
and two dips.
Above the base formats sits a line-up of "Pimped Up" pita pockets, each themed around a different place:
the house Sabbaba Pita Pocket ($20) with the full four-salad, four-dip combo; a Larnaca pocket ($19.90)
with olives, green chilli and shredded halloumi; an Algerian pocket ($19.90) built on chickpeas and
eggplant; a Tunisian pocket ($20) with Marrakech salad and sweet potato; and a Cancun pocket ($21.90)
that goes full Tex-Mex with salsa, sour cream, guacamole, jalapeños, corn chips and cheese. The
most-liked item on the whole menu, by Uber Eats' own "percent liked" metric, is the Sabbaba Pita Pocket
at 89% approval across 554 ratings, followed closely by the Plate at 90% across 996 ratings.
Salads are sold individually too, mostly $10–14: a cauliflower-and-avocado salad, plain pickles, a vegan
tabouli, red cabbage in a sweet-and-sour dressing, crunchy edamame, and a lentil-quinoa-haloumi salad.
On the sides menu, the Hot Chips ($10, described as "famous" and lightly seasoned) and Six Falafel
($10.90, 89% liked) look like the standout add-ons, alongside haloumi chips with tzatziki, chicken
shawarma and chicken shish. A can of soft drink is $4.50.
Four menu sections exist on the Uber Eats page — Pita Packs, Dips/Condiments & Extras, Desserts, and
Drinks — but returned no items when this was pulled, which is almost certainly a scraping gap rather than an
empty menu (a $4.50 soft drink can, for instance, showed up under "Featured" but logically belongs in Drinks). A
full, current price list from the owner would close this gap far more reliably than re-scraping the delivery app.
What Customers Are Saying
The picture that emerges depends a lot on which platform you're reading. Uber Eats shows a very strong
4.6 out of 5 across more than 3,000 ratings, though it only surfaces 17 written comments, and every one of
them is 5 stars — reviewers there call out "great food and good value," praise it as "the best falafel and
chicken pitas in Bondi," and one recent reviewer went as far as calling it "the best food I've ordered off
Uber Eats in Sydney by far."
Google tells a more mixed story for the same address: 3.8 out of 5 across 188 ratings. The handful of
review texts available lean positive on service and on the salads and hummus specifically — two reviewers
name staff members ("manzil" and "twinkle") for good service, and one recommends the lamb pita for halal
diners — but two others raise real concerns: one found the grilled meat under-seasoned and "not smokey
enough," and another said the $18 plate "tasted good but the place did not seem hygienic." That's a
notable gap worth taking seriously rather than averaging away.
For brand-level context (not the Spring Street store specifically), the original Bondi Beach location sits at
4.1 out of 5 on TripAdvisor across 102 reviews, ranked #6 of 30 "quick bites" in the area. The range there
is wide — five-star reviews call it "authentically Middle Eastern" and praise the lamb shish and shawarma,
while critical reviews mention a cleanliness lapse ("food scraps all over the floor"), an overdone lamb
shish, and — in one 2019 review — a foreign object found in a falafel order that was refunded on the spot.
Vegan and vegetarian diners consistently rate the falafel and salad options well across HappyCow and


abillion, both of which describe the Bondi Junction options as "clearly defined" for plant-based eaters.
Read together, the consistent strengths across every platform are the falafel, the salads/dips (hummus,
tahini, babaganoush), and value for money at a $ price point. The consistent soft spots are grilled-meat
seasoning/doneness and, occasionally, cleanliness — both worth the owner's attention regardless of
which platform surfaced them.
A few representative comments, as written:
"Honestly the best food I've ordered off uber eats in Sydney by far. Insane quality and taste." — Uber
Eats, 12 Jul 2025
"Had the plate. Well priced at around $18... but the place did not seem hygienic." — Google, undated
"Stumbled across sabbaba and the smell was amazing... we really loved it. We will be back!" —
TripAdvisor, Sep 2023
"Falafel was crunchy also tasty! Pita was fluffy." — HappyCow, Sep 2024
Everything Else on the Uber Eats Page
Beyond the menu, hours and reviews already covered, the store page carries a handful of platform-level
details worth keeping. Uber Eats' internal store ID for this listing is
f8b5ecba-2b13-4479-97f6-af8d416dd32b. Oddly, the page's own breadcrumb trail files the store under
Australia > New South Wales > Sydney > Bondi Beach > Sabbaba — not Bondi Junction, which is the
address actually listed. That lines up with the earlier note about the store description text also saying
"Bondi Beach": it looks like Uber Eats has this listing tagged with a neighbourhood template built for the
Hall Street / Campbell Parade store rather than Spring Street.
On ordering: the page offers a "Group order" option for shared carts, shows a "$0 delivery fee (new users)"
banner, and its FAQ mentions Uber One membership as a way to get $0 delivery on select orders going
forward. Payment runs entirely through the customer's Uber Eats account, and ordering itself happens
either in the Uber Eats app or on the website — there's no separate direct-order link for this store. At the
time this was pulled, the page showed delivery as unavailable ("too far to deliver," "available at 11:00 am")
— that reflects the browsing session's location, not a permanent property of the store, so it's worth
re-checking live from an address near Bondi Junction.
On photos: the only image the static page exposes is a single store cover photo (used for both the page
header and the social-share/meta image). Individual menu items only get photos inside an on-page modal
that Uber Eats loads with JavaScript when a shopper clicks an item — that content isn't present in the
page's underlying markup, so it can't be pulled without an actual browser session driving the site.
The store page's own FAQ, in full:
Can I order Sabbaba delivery in Sydney with Uber Eats?
Yes. Sabbaba delivery is available on Uber Eats in Sydney.
Is Sabbaba delivery available near me?
Enter your address to see if Sabbaba delivery is available to your location in Sydney.
How do I order Sabbaba delivery online in Sydney?


There are 2 ways to place an order on Uber Eats: on the app or online using the Uber Eats website. After
looking over the menu, choose your items, add them to your cart, then review, place, and track your order.
Where can I find Sabbaba online menu prices?
Upfront pricing for Sabbaba's items is shown directly on the store page.
How do I get free delivery on my Sabbaba order?
An Uber One membership, where available, includes a $0 delivery fee on select orders.
How do I pay for my Sabbaba order?
Payment is handled via the customer's Uber Eats account.
What's the best thing to order for Sabbaba delivery in Sydney?
The FAQ points shoppers to the items shown in "Picked for you" on the store page.


Open Questions for the Business Owner
This section is meant to be handed to the owner directly — a short list of things only they can confirm,
written as plain questions rather than data-quality jargon.
1
What is the exact shopfront address (street number and shop number) for Spring Street, Bondi
Junction? Sources disagree between 77, 91, and a 71–91 range.
2
What are the current, correct weekly opening hours — including any public-holiday hours? Google and
Uber Eats currently show conflicting schedules for the same store.
3
Is the Westfield / Oxford Street listing a separate Sabbaba, or the same business under a different
entrance/floor reference?
4
Are the Spring Street, Westfield, and Bondi Beach locations under common ownership, a franchise
arrangement, or fully independent operators? This affects whether an AI/agentic build should be
scoped to a single store or the whole brand.
5
Can you provide a current, complete menu with prices — including the Pita Packs, Dips/Condiments,
Desserts and Drinks sections, which returned no items in this pass?
6
Do you actively monitor and respond to Google reviews? The Google rating (3.8) is notably lower than
Uber Eats (4.6) for the same store, and it's worth understanding why.
7
Is sabbaba.com.au actively maintained? It couldn't be crawled for this profile (it blocks automated
access) so its current menu/hours/contact info is unverified here.
8
What delivery platforms are you currently active on, beyond Uber Eats?
Sources: Uber Eats storefront page, Google Places, TripAdvisor, Yelp, HappyCow, abillion, Wanderlog, Time
Out Sydney. Compiled 4 September 2026 for internal use as a phase-1 training/testing dataset. Not an official
statement from Sabbaba's ownership — all facts above should be verified with the business before being relied
on operationally.
